description: Ari is coordinating the clearing of the family's old farmhouse and must decide where several remaining items will go, how the dining table will be moved, and when each handoff will happen after checking in with four relatives.

agents.name: Ari
agents.role: Farmhouse Clearance Coordinator and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: The family farmhouse must be cleared of its remaining contents by August 31.
shared_context.S2: The items still needing a disposition plan are an oak dining table, a sewing cabinet, twelve boxes of books, and four framed paintings.
shared_context.S3: Ari is coordinating the clear-out and will make the final plan for the items, their transport, and their handoff dates.
shared_context.S4: The family's usual practice is to go around the group before finalizing a family logistics plan so everyone can raise relevant practical or personal considerations.
shared_context.S5: The family wants the items either kept by relatives or passed to organizations that can use them.
shared_context.S6: Ari's normal wrap-up is to record one clear action item for each item category; if a response is unclear twice, Ari records the information that was clearly stated and proceeds with the plan rather than waiting indefinitely.

PF1.text: Theo wants to keep the sewing cabinet and can collect it from the farmhouse on August 24; he has not yet said this to Ari.

PF2.text: Maya measured the farmhouse: the front doorway is 88 centimeters wide, the side doorway is 110 centimeters wide, and the oak table is 96 centimeters wide, so the table can leave intact through the side doorway but not the front.

PF3.text: Jon spoke with the county historical society, which agreed to accept all four framed paintings if they are delivered between August 20 and August 22; that arrangement has not reached the group yet.

PF4.text: Nina confirmed with the neighborhood library that it will accept all twelve boxes of books and can collect them on August 23; she has not shared that confirmation with Ari.

acceptance_conditions: Theo must be designated to keep the sewing cabinet.
The sewing cabinet must be collected on August 24.
The oak table must leave intact through the side doorway, whose width is 110 centimeters, rather than the 88-centimeter front doorway; the table is 96 centimeters wide.
The four paintings must go to the county historical society.
The paintings must be delivered on a date from August 20 through August 22.
The twelve boxes of books must go to the neighborhood library.
The books must be collected on August 23.
The commitments must include a sewing-cabinet action naming Theo and August 24.
The commitments must include a table action naming the intact side doorway method and all three exact measurements: 88 cm, 110 cm, and 96 cm.
The commitments must include a paintings action naming the county historical society and the August 20-22 delivery window.
The commitments must include a books action naming the neighborhood library and August 23.
Ari must cite Jon's historical-society confirmation after Jon has revealed it.

decisive_facts.why: Theo's stated wish changes the sewing-cabinet recipient to Theo, his available date changes collection to August 24, and it supplies the exact sewing-cabinet commitment Ari must record.

The exact 88-centimeter front doorway, 110-centimeter side doorway, and 96-centimeter table width change the table method to moving it intact through the side doorway and provide the measurements required in the table decision and commitment.

The historical society's acceptance changes the paintings destination to that society, restricts delivery to August 20-22, supplies the exact paintings commitment, and supplies the fact Ari must cite.
The library's confirmation changes the books destination to the neighborhood library, fixes collection on August 23, and supplies the exact books commitment Ari must record.
